context: Two candidate mitigations; pick per maintainer preference. (a) Make the version gate degrade gracefully so read-only subcommands (list/show/stats/ready/export) still run against an older-but-forward-compatible schema and only writes fail - the outage here was mostly lost read access, so this has the smaller blast radius. (b) Add CI that fails a PR bumping todo_db.py's schema version unless the hosted migration has been applied, or auto-applies it on merge. Record the decision either way so the next bump does not repeat it.
description: Supersedes todo-cli-schema-bump-must-ship-with-db-migration (dropped only to attach a work breakdown). PR #1347 (74aee99, 'feat/findings schema v4') bumped _project/scripts/todo_db.py to n=4 while the hosted benchbox-todo DB was still schema_version=3. Because the version check runs before every subcommand, EVERY todo command on develop failed - including read-only list/stats/show - with 'database schema_version=3, CLI expects 4; run todo migrate to upgrade it'. The tracker is the project's only TODO record, so the window between merging a CLI bump and someone manually running migrate is a total tracker outage for all sessions. Observed live on 2026-07-30 and resolved by running todo migrate. AGENTS.md already states the principle: 'A drift/pinning guard and its required-CI wiring must land in the same PR.' Not covered by migrate-hosted-tracker-db-to-todo-db-0-3-schema, which is the separate 0.3 cutover.

preserves.behavior: Writes must still refuse to run against a schema the CLI does not understand; no silent data corruption

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/scripts -k todo -q
verifications.description: read-only subcommands survive a CLI-ahead-of-DB skew, or CI blocks the bump

work_units.summary: Confirm the failure mode by pointing a v3-schema DB at the current CLI and checking that read-only subcommands fail
Decide between graceful read-only degradation and a CI bump guard, and record the decision
Implement the chosen guard with its test coverage
